message.content:
At a pressure of 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) water’s freezing (melting) point is only slightly above the standard 0 °C.  
Using the known phase‑diagram data (triple point at 0.01 °C/611 Pa and 0 °C/101 325 Pa) the melting temperature at 10 kPa works out to roughly **+0.009 °C** – i.e., essentially 0 °C within experimental uncertainty.
